## How the dimensions earned PASS

### tests

PV-1 carries 9 BLOCKER-severity pass criteria, all confirmed at the phase boundary. The two substantive scripts each carry their own fixture-driven selftest suite:

- `verdict_findings_parity.py --selftest` returned 11/11 PASS (latency 25 ms, well inside the 250 ms NFR-1 budget).
- `audit_op11_adr_parity.py --selftest` returned 6/6 PASS.

The remaining PV-1 criteria are grep-anchored or frontmatter-inspection assertions, each empirically re-corroborated at the phase boundary (see Pass-criteria status below).

PV-1.C8's AC-CC-2-g pre-feature checkpoint resume smoke is explicitly deferred to T4.6 per the phase-validators spec; this is recorded as MAJOR-deferred per the spec's own qualifier, NOT as a Phase 1 BLOCKER.

### audits

`detect_stubs.py` reported zero findings across all 9 tasks. The two new Python scripts (`verdict_findings_parity.py`, `audit_op11_adr_parity.py`) carry no code stubs, no FIXME / TODO markers, no `NotImplementedError`, and no `assert True` / `assert False` sole-assertion patterns. `audits_stub` is `false` this phase — detect_stubs ran directly via each task's quality handler, no coordinator-stub path was exercised, so the Q-CC-4 stub-vs-real distinction does not apply.

### validator

`validate_adr_placement.py` passed on both new ADRs (PV-1.C1 + PV-1.C2). The pre-existing `validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py` gap — its dispatcher lacks an `adrs/` early-return to `validate_adr_frontmatter`, causing it to emit MAJOR findings against every ADR in the repo — is carried forward from the Phase 0 baseline as informational, not a new finding. Phase 1 introduces zero new frontmatter regressions; both ADR-0057 v1.0.1 and ADR-0058 v1.0.0 carry conformant frontmatter when read through the correct validator path.

### discipline

The 4-phase quality discipline executed cleanly on both substantive Python scripts. The SKILL.md edits (T1.6 / T1.7 / T1.8) passed structural + grep-based L1/L2/L3 checks at each of the 9 wire-in sites. Zero NEEDS_REVISION cycles consumed across any task.

### scope_deviations

Two informational items, both flagged but non-blocking:

1. **T1.8 sibling-content absorption.** The T1.8 edit absorbed adjacent T1.6 / T1.7 SKILL.md content in the same write. T1.8's task quality handler verified the absorbed content matches each absorbed task's spec verbatim (grep-anchored counts came back as expected: `scope_class >= 2`, `verdict_findings_parity.py == 9`, FR-2 self-check markers `>= 1`). Recorded as informational per ADR-0033 scope-deviation surfacing, NOT drift.

2. **Pre-existing systemic frontmatter validator gap.** Carried forward from Phase 0; not introduced by Phase 1. The canonical PV-1 placement check uses `validate_adr_placement.py`, which passes. The project-wide `validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py` tooling gap is out of scope for this feature.
